nodes.label: Android Density Bucket Ladder
nodes.rationale: Measured sizes 48/72/96/144/192 px form the canonical 1x/1.5x/2x/3x/4x Android scale ladder off a 48dp baseline. Android resolves `@mipmap/ic_launcher` by matching the device's screen density to the nearest bucket, so the five files are one logical asset pre-rasterized per bucket, not five distinct icons. Trade-off: raster-per-density costs APK size and must be regenerated in lockstep on any art change, but it avoids runtime scaling blur on the launcher surface.

nodes.label: Missing Adaptive Icon Configuration
nodes.rationale: A filesystem sweep for adaptive-icon assets found only these five legacy PNGs — no mipmap-anydpi-v26/ic_launcher.xml, no separate foreground/background layers, no monochrome layer. On Android 8.0+ launchers the flat PNG is therefore wrapped in a system-supplied shape and cannot participate in mask shaping, parallax, or themed (Material You) icons. AMBIGUOUS as an intentional choice: consistent with untouched Flutter scaffolding rather than a considered legacy-only decision.

nodes.label: Unreplaced Flutter Default Branding
nodes.rationale: All five launcher icons are the stock Flutter 'F' chevron logo (light blue #54C5F8 upper stroke, mid blue over a dark navy #01579B fold) on transparent, shipped verbatim by `flutter create`. They were never replaced with app-specific artwork for this Turkish Quran translation (kuran_turkce_meal) app. Consequence: on-device the app is visually indistinguishable from every other unbranded Flutter project, and store submission would surface it as generic. Design intent is therefore absent rather than deliberate — this is scaffolding residue, not a branding decision.
